Elena — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciate the level of detail. High-level responses below; I also attached a draft Private Addendum and operator attestation template for your review.

1) Deliverables: Redwood will deliver the following as part of the Private Addendum:
   - Deployment artifacts: signed runbook (exportable PDF), scheduled snapshot manifest (hash list), and an encrypted snapshot transfer procedure.
   - Operator access telemetry: short-lived console access windows (timeboxed, JTIs logged), session recordings retained for N days per the Order Form.
   - Attestations: a signed operator attestation confirming no persistent remote admin accounts and a custody transfer checklist when snapshots are provided.

2) Audit window & logs: we can provide a standard 30-day audit window for on-site or remote review; for PulseHealth's auditors we can extend to a 45-day window by exception. We keep trace-level logs for 90 days by default; longer retention can be added as an SLA add-on.

3) Escrow-like continuity: we do not do traditional source-code escrow, but we offer a 'proof-of-access' snapshot + signed handover package together with an operator runbook and an operator container image (where permitted). That package is sufficient to restore service in a cold-start scenario; if you need a sealed-deposit escrow we can work with a third-party escrow vendor (adds time/cost).

Proposed timeline (post-orderform execution):
- Week 0: Order form executes + PO.
- Week 1-2: Redwood legal finalizes Private Addendum redlines (we aim to accept most of your annotated items).
- Week 3: Delivery of initial evidence package (runbook, snapshot manifest, attestation template).

Next steps: 1) Please confirm which of the three escrow paths (standard evidence package | evidence + 3rd-party escrow | custom sealed-deposit) you prefer, 2) any mandatory retention periods or auditor contact, and 3) whether PulseHealth requires on-prem witness certification (we have process notes in the attached draft).

I've attached: Redwood_PrivateAddendum_draft_20280216.pdf and Operator_Attestation_template.docx.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Elena's note and my quick responses. Need legal/contract sign-off on two discrete areas before I send the formal redline:

A) License scope carve: Elena's team expects a statement that licensed models and artifacts supplied under the Private Addendum are for internal PulseHealth production use only and cannot be redistributed. We should confirm the exact permitted use language and any audit rights carveouts.

B) Proof-of-access vs escrow: I'm proposing we keep our standard evidence package (runbooks, snapshot manifests, signed attestation) as the base. If they insist on a sealed-deposit escrow we should require: (i) 3rd-party escrow vendor agreed up front, (ii) deposit of packaged artifacts only (not source or model weights unless contractually required), and (iii) clearly limited reactivation rights tied to defined breach/insolvency events.

Marissa — can Solutions validate that the attestation template and snapshot manifest provide sufficient operational handoff for a cold-start restore? Markus/Laura — please advise on minimal changes to language so we don't open broad redistribution or operational-control obligations.

Thanks,
Jonas
